# polyweave

> A Claude Code plugin that makes a game's parts. It sits between Claude Code and the tools
> that make game content (Blender, Godot and AI generators such as Meshy, FLUX, Ideogram,
> ElevenLabs and sfxr), checks every result against the bar the project sets, and puts the
> best candidates on a review page where a person approves what ships. It makes 3D models,
> images, music, sound effects, visual effects, voices, words, levels, animation and
> ready-made game kits. It runs on the developer's own machine, against files in their own
> repository: no account, no hosted service.

## For agents

This site answers a coding agent in files it can grep. Every route has a Markdown twin
beside it, the same page converted from the same render, with the navigation, the footer
and the call to action dropped. Read `<route>/index.md` instead of the HTML: the landing
page is [`/index.md`](https://alegauss.github.io/polyweave/index.md). The routes, their
twins and their byte sizes are in
[`manifest.json`](https://alegauss.github.io/polyweave/manifest.json).

## Install

```
pip install git+https://github.com/alegauss/polyweave
/plugin marketplace add alegauss/polyweave
/plugin install polyweave@polyweave
```

The plugin brings one MCP server (`python -m polyweave serve`), the skill that teaches
Claude Code to drive it, and its hooks. Python 3.11 or newer; Blender and Godot are
optional, and `capabilities()` says which tools this machine has.

## What Claude Code gains

- **Hands on every tool**: Blender, Godot and the 3D, picture, sound and voice generators
  through one set of calls.
- **Eyes and ears**: a render returns its measurements (silhouette, colour, contrast, how
  it reads at display size); a sound returns loudness, clipping and loop seams.
- **A bar to aim at**: an acceptance spec per part (`<asset>.accept.toml`), a list of named
  predicates over a closed measurement vocabulary, and a search that tunes the permitted
  parameters until every predicate passes, returning a contact sheet and a trace.
- **Hands on the game**: open it, send input, wait for a state, take screenshots and
  replay a run, headless.
- **A person's verdict**: candidates go to a review page and the call waits for the
  answer. An agent never accepts or rejects its own look.
- **Errors that carry the fix**: a stable code, a message with no traceback, and a
  `remedy` that is the call which closes it.
- **Memory across sessions**: anything slow returns a handle whose state is a file under
  `.polyweave/`, so the next session can pick it up.
- **Self-describing tools**: `describe()` lists each parameter's type, range and default.
- **A budget**: a spending ceiling a person sets once in `polyweave.toml`, with every
  spend quoted and written in a ledger.
- **Provenance**: every artefact records the model, prompt, seed, cost and licence that
  made it; credits are written from that record.
- **Kits**: menus, settings, saves, input, co-op and accessibility, installed into a
  project already tested.

## Non-goals

The roadmap governs these, and the landing page carries each one: a graphical editor;
replacing Blender, Godot or the generative service; spending money on the agent's own
judgement; one project's palette, rig or paths compiled in; a hosted service or an account;
an agent accepting or rejecting its own look; one genre's level format built in; writing a
game's story for it.

## Layout

- `src/polyweave`: the plugin, in Python. `plugin/`: what Claude Code installs.
- `docs/specs/`: the contracts more than one feature depends on.
- `docs/ROADMAP.md`, `docs/CHANGELOG.md`, `docs/IMPROVEMENTS.md`: governed by
  [roadkeep](https://github.com/alegauss/roadkeep). What is still open is in the roadmap.
- `site/`: this site.
